display.title: True Ahavas Yisroel, Part 2
display.summary_short: Why Cheshvan is called Mar Cheshvan and Bul, then two more stories Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev told about the secret generosity of David, the 'stingy' rich man.
display.summary_long: In the month of Cheshvan of a Hakhel year, the storyteller explains the month's names: Mar Cheshvan for its first raindrops, or for its bitterness at having no Yom Tov, and Bul, the month when Shlomo HaMelech finished the Beis HaMikdash. Because its dedication waited until Tishrei, Hashem promised that the third Beis HaMikdash will be celebrated in Cheshvan. After a short recap of last week, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev tells his second story. Chaim, a poor man, wants to travel to seek his fortune and tricks his wife into agreeing by claiming that David will pay her his wages every Thursday. When she comes, David quietly tells his secretary to pay her every week. Chaim returns rich and tries to repay, but David refuses: it was his own tzedakah. In the third story, a factory owner borrows a thousand rubles and names Hashem as his guarantor. When he comes a few weeks late to repay, David says his guarantor has already paid. Each time Rabbi Levi Yitzchak rules for David, showing that every Jew may be a hidden tzaddik.
display.lesson: Look at every Jew with a good eye; you never know how great he really is. Loving one another brings the Geulah closer.
